responses.text: Agreed; the README was wrong at n = 2^31. The Narrowings bullet on n + BLOCK_SIZE <= 2^31 now gives each excluded range its own reason. (1) n > 2^31: every covered BLOCK_SIZE divides 2^31, so the last program has pid >= 2^31 / BLOCK_SIZE and its int32 product pid * BLOCK_SIZE wraps (BLOCK_SIZE = 1024, n = 2^31 + 1: pid = 2^21, pid * BLOCK_SIZE = -2^31); its enabled lanes access memory before the buffers (out of bounds), and from n > 2^32 on some programs' offsets wrap onto other programs' elements. (2) n = 2^31: nothing wraps (the largest offset is 2^31 - 1), the indexing is exact; the size is excluded because Triton passes n_elements = 2^31 as int64 while the model takes n_elements : I32 (IntV.ofNat n, map entry for lines 30-36), so it would need another model. (3) 2^31 - BLOCK_SIZE < n < 2^31: exact indexing, excluded by Block.Fits (library issue L8), as before. The Conditions table's row for n_fits now names the same three reasons. Following the round's notes, remark (2), the overlap row now says 'can make programs race', and the Aliasing narrowing says the conditions are on whole buffers (Buf.bytes), so they also exclude a harmless overlap lying only in elements from n on. Only README.md changed; the Lean, the map and the manifest are unchanged, so the gate b7289baba9114347 is current.
